title: carMetrics sets a flat carousel's gap once
Tell a failed paint from a dropped one, so callers stop retrying and polling
body:
## Summary
Raster.run resolves null both when a job is dropped by its tag and when it failed to paint, so callers cannot tell a retry-worthy drop from a permanent failure.

## Description
app/_landing/cosmos/engine/raster.ts:139-142 (worker 'fail') and :220 (main catch) resolve the same null as drop() at :161-167. Consumers: app/_landing/cosmos/engine/carousel.ts:112-114 resets `c._q = false` on null, so a card whose diorama throws is re-queued by ensureArt on every glide frame (placeCards -> ensureArt) for as long as the carousel moves; app/_landing/cosmos/engine/worlds.ts:75-77 marks a world `done` on null and never sets cx.worldReady, so app/_landing/cosmos/engine/nav.ts:31-34 tryCover re-arms a 100 ms timeout for as long as the level is open. Fixed looks like: Painted | 'dropped' | 'failed' (or a `failed` flag), carousel keeps `_q` on failure, worlds lands an empty world (or reports) on failure.

## Flow
- seed a diorama op that throws (e.g. an id whose motif is missing)
- open a type with >3 templates and glide
- count raster.run calls for that card per frame: 1 per frame today
- open a type in lite tier with a world job that fails: tryCover timeouts fire at 10 Hz until the level changes

## Expected impact
Only a visitor whose browser fails a paint notices (a stuck overview behind a world that never lands). What could break: a dropped job misread as failed would never repaint.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a failed paint is not retried every frame and does not leave a 10 Hz poll running
Before: raster.run calls per glide frame for a failing card: 1 (walked: carousel.ts:31 -> :85 -> :112); tryCover re-arms: unbounded at 10 Hz
After: 0 retries after the first failure; tryCover stops (lands or gives up)
Method: simulation - three walked paths (carousel retry, world cover poll, library tile which already does not retry); the probe needs a fake cx for carousel.ts and nav.ts (shell context) that this round did not build
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: tests/next-server/landing-cosmos-engine.test.ts: a fake raster whose run() resolves 'failed'; count ensureArt re-queues over 10 placeCards frames (syncCarousel) and tryCover timeouts over 1 s (nav.ts, shell context - needs its owner)

title: Read the category rect before hotCat's class writes, not after
body:
## Summary
hotCat adds two classes and then reads area.getBoundingClientRect(), forcing a synchronous style+layout on every category hover, before showBanner forces its own.

## Description
app/_landing/cosmos/engine/library.ts:141-143 writes b.classList.add('hot') and area.classList.add('hasHot') and then reads area.getBoundingClientRect(); showBanner (app/_landing/cosmos/engine/banner.ts) then writes the name and reads offsetWidth. Two forced layouts per hover where one would do: the area's rect does not depend on the hot classes' paint. Fixed: read the rect first, then write.

## Flow
- open a family with several categories
- hover a tile: hotCat writes classes, reads rect (layout 1), showBanner writes name, reads size (layout 2)

## Expected impact
Hover latency on the family sheet; the counter is forced layouts per hover. Could break: if a hot class changes the area's box, the banner centre moves by that delta.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - forced layouts per category hover
Before: 2 (walked: library.ts:141-143 then banner.ts:180)
After: 1
Method: simulation - hotCat is reachable only through buildLib's handlers, which need a fake DOM for the whole sheet; the layout-counting fake built this round for showBanner is the instrument to extend
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: extend the layout-counting fake document in tests/next-server/landing-cosmos-engine.test.ts to drive openFam -> a .cat onpointerenter and count forced layouts

title: Stop placeCards querying .dur and restyling hidden cards every glide frame
body:
## Summary
placeCards runs a querySelector('.dur') per card per frame and rewrites transform, opacity, z-index and two custom properties on cards that are hidden.

## Description
app/_landing/cosmos/engine/carousel.ts:18-35: for every card on every carousel frame, five style writes, a classList.toggle and c.querySelector('.dur'), including cards with q.o <= 0.01 that are visibility:hidden. The .dur node is fixed at build (carousel.ts:176) and can be held. Card's type lives in state.ts (landing-cosmos-shell), so caching it on the card needs that context or a WeakMap here.

## Flow
- open a type with N templates
- drag the carousel: each frame runs N querySelector calls and 6N style writes

## Expected impact
Frame cost while gliding a long carousel; measured as DOM calls per frame. Could break: a hidden card that becomes visible must get a fresh pose on that frame.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - DOM queries and style writes per glide frame
Before: N querySelector + 6N writes per frame (walked)
After: 0 querySelector; writes only for visible cards plus the visibility flip
Method: simulation - placeCards is private; syncCarousel reaches it with a fake cx, not built this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a fake cx with N recording card objects driven through syncCarousel(cx, i); count querySelector and style writes per call

title: Promote a prewarmed world to the open world's priority when it is opened
body:
## Summary
buildWorld adopts a prewarm still queued at priority 3 instead of raising it to the -1 an opened world gets, so it waits behind queued tiles.

## Description
app/_landing/cosmos/engine/worlds.ts:131-133 reuses cx.worldPre when its key matches; paintWorld queued it at prio 3 (worlds.ts:87), behind library tiles at prio 1+k (library.ts:105) that openFam queued first. raster.ts has no way to re-prioritise a queued job. Fixed: Raster.bump(tag, prio) and buildWorld bumps 'prewarm' to -1 when it adopts one.

## Flow
- open a family with many categories (tiles queued prio 1..n, then prewarm prio 3)
- click a category before the tiles drain: the world's job sits behind tiles 0..2

## Expected impact
Time to world on a fast click; usually zero because tiles drain in the ~1 s before a click. Could break: re-sorting the queue mid-flight.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - jobs painted ahead of an opened world
Before: up to 3 queued tiles + 2 in flight (walked)
After: 0 queued ahead (2 in flight remain)
Method: simulation - the queue order is probe-able with the recording Worker built this round; not built for want of a realistic case where tiles are still queued at click time
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: FakeWorker in tests/next-server/landing-cosmos-engine.test.ts: queue 6 'lib' jobs then a 'prewarm' at 3, adopt it, read the posted order
